observations:
Torah #30 contains five packages formed from 34 bechina edges across 52 nodes (18 raw connected components, merged to 5 packages). The analysis did not uncover a sixth independent domain meeting the threshold of 3+ bechina-connected concepts forming a self-contained cluster.

The primary candidate for a new package was the 'or hapanim / simcha / chayyim' cluster — the light of the divine countenance that the malkhut must be elevated toward through the festivals. The source text invokes this in bechina language ('be'or pnei melekh chayyim'; 'lev same'ach yeitiv panim') repeatedly. However, in the dataset these connections are encoded as eitza (cause-and-effect) rather than bechina for reference=30. The festivals PRODUCE the or-hapanim, and simcha PRODUCES the or-panim — these are directional flows rather than shared-nature equivalences. Therefore no new bechina package is warranted for this cluster.

A second candidate was the 'azut diqdushah / reception of Torah / standing in prayer' cluster. The source discusses azut diqdushah as necessary for both Torah-reception and prayer. However, in the dataset the ref=30 edges involving azut are exclusively eitza (edges 2589, 2596, 2701 ref=30, type=eitza). Only one bechina statement is implicit in the source text (that azut = bechina of 'the Israelites are brazen/azzin' who received Torah), but this is not encoded as a distinct bechina triplet in the dataset.

A third candidate was a 'gevina / two toroth' cluster based on the riddle-answer structure of the Torah (terei gevinei = two kinds of cheese = two kinds of Torah). However, the gevinei concept is elaborated through eitza in the dataset rather than via bechina edges pointing to ref=30.

Conclusion: All bechina-connected concepts in Torah #30 are adequately captured within the five proposed packages. The main structural domains are: (1) lower intellect / malkhut, (2) festivals / knowing the times, (3) tzaddik-mashiach / prayers / rebuke, (4) four sons / four kingdoms taxonomy, (5) evil counterpart — foreign toroth / dross. These five packages map cleanly onto the Torah's five-part argument: [malkhut needing elevation] → [via festivals] → [through the tzaddik's rebuke] → [calibrated to the four-son types of each person] → [distinguishing holy from foreign Torah].
